title: Performance drift inspector, load-harness archival store, and triage UX
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a coherent system that archives per-run load/benchmark results, provides an orthogonal comparison UI (tokens/sec, p95/p99, cost-per-token, memory snapshots, kv-cache hit rate) and surfaces an actionable anomaly triage workflow (auto-suspect attribution and reproducible reruns). This ticket covers the archival schema, comparison view wireframes, anomaly fingerprinting algorithm, and the triage playbook + integrations to the replay runner.
acceptance_criteria: Archival store accepts standardized run payloads (metadata + metrics + optional heap/memory snapshot + sample traces) and can be queried by run-id, model, commit, and workload fingerprint

Comparison UI shows side-by-side and delta views for tokens/sec, p95, p99, mean latency, cost-per-token, and kv cache hit rate with the ability to pin three runs and highlight statistically significant regressions
Automated triage suggestions produced for top-3 likely causes (kernel change, batching shift, input distribution drift) with confidence score and links to failing sample prompts
A reproducible replay can be launched from the UI that runs a subset of the original workload with identical seq-length distribution and seed and records results back to the archival store
Alerting hooks emit structured regression events to PagerDuty/Slack with a link to the triage card and rerun button
notes: Prefer append-only immutable run objects to simplify diffs and reproducibility
Store large artifacts (heap dump, full traces) on object storage and reference from archival record to avoid DB bloat
We will canonicalize metrics names (tokens_per_sec, p95_ms, p99_ms, cost_per_token_usd, kv_hit_ratio) to make cross-run comparisons robust
Design trade-off: compute fingerprint server-side (fast) vs client-side (reproducible) — decided to compute deterministic fingerprint in both places and reconcile
We should avoid heavy ML-based triage initially — start with heuristics + rules and collect labels for future classifier training
decisions: Schema: single top-level run record with versioned payload (v1) and pointer to artifacts on S3
UI: orthogonal diff mode (metric delta + waterfall) prioritized over heatmap in first iteration
Anomaly detection: change detection using Bootstrap confidence intervals + thresholded relative change; annotate with root-cause heuristics
Replays: constrained to 10% sample of original workload for quick local validation; ability to request full replay as an expensive job
